sentences.text:
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the revisionist as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material on record.

This criminal revision has been filed with a prayer to allow the application of the revisionist and quash the order dated 11.01.2024 passed by learned Additional Session Judge, Court No. 1, Rampur,
in Session Trial No. 330 of 2021 arising from Case Crime No. 210 of 2021 under Sections 498A,
304B, 323, 504 of I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Milak, District Rampur and also further prayed to direct the learned Additional Session Judge Court No. 1, Rampur to summon the opposite party nos. 2 to 4 for the offence committed by them.

sentences.text:
It is submitted by learned counsel for the revisionist that in this case the revisionist lodged an F.I.R.
against the opposite party nos. 2, 3, 4 and the husband of the deceased for demand of dowry and harassment on account of which she committed suicide by taking poison.
During the course of investigation the names of opposite party nos. 2, 3 and 4 those were minor Devar and Nanad and Atar Singh (Mamia Sasur) were exonerated.

During the trial statement of P.W. 1 informant (father of the deceased) and P.W. 2 (mother of the deceased) were recorded in which though P.W. 1 turned hostile but P.W. 2 (mother of the deceased) supported the prosecution version.

Thereafter an application under Section 319 Cr.P.C. was moved by the revisionist before the learned trial court to summon the opposite parties for trial but it was rejected without considering the material on record and the statement as made by P.W. 2 (mother of the deceased) which cannot be said to be lawful,
therefore request to set it aside the order passed by learned trial court on an application under Section 319 Cr.P.C. and to allow the revision.

Learned A.G.A. contended that in this case P.W. 1 who was informant and father of the deceased did not support the prosecution version before the learned trial court when his statement was recorded,
as a result his cross-examination was made by the learned Prosecutor even then he did not support the prosecution case.
P.W. 2 supported the prosecution version.
The learned trial court considered the material on record and the statements made by P.W. 1 and P.W. 2 and rejected the application.
There is no any illegality or impropriety in the order passed by the learned trial court but this revision being devoid of merit is liable to be dismissed.

On considering the facts and circumstances, submissions made by learned counsel for the revisionist as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, it appears that the deceased committed suicide by consuming poison.
As per viscera report organophosphorus insecticide poison was found.

In the F.I.R. allegation of demand of dowry and harassment was made by the informant P.W. 1 against the husband and his other relatives including opposite party no. 2 and 3, minor brother and sister of the husband and opposite party no. 3 Mamia Sasur resident of another village.
During the course of investigation the complicity of opposite party no. 2, 3, and 4 was also found not established, as a result they were exonerated.

During the trial court statement of informant (father of the deceased) as P.W. 1 was recorded in which he did not support the prosecution version but stated clearly that people in sasural did not beat her and there was no any Panchayat prior to the alleged incident and they did not cause death of his daughter on account of demand of dowry.
At this stage he was declared to be hostile and cross-examination was made by learned Prosecutor in which he did not support the statement as made by him before the I.O. under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

When cross-examined by learned counsel for the opposite party he again stated that his daughter never told him about demand of Rs. 3 lakhs and bullet motorcycle by the accused persons and she was never subjected to torture in that regard.

The deceased was mentally depressed and was being treated by Dr. Tarun Agarwal at Moradabad in Ruhalkhand, Bareilly but on account of illness she was under distress and due to that illness she consumed poison.
P.W. 2 (mother of the deceased) who was also examined in which she supported the prosecution version.

sentences.text: From the statements made by P.W. 1 (father of the deceased) and P.W. 2 (mother of the deceased), it appears that statements of both the witnesses are contradictory on the basis of which it cannot be said to be established that there was a demand of dowry or harassment on the part of opposite parties with the deceased, as a result she consumed poison but for some other ulterior motive present application has been moved on the part of revisionist against the opposite parties those were minor and relatives of the husband of the deceased.
It is to note that Court cannot be allowed to become a tool for misusing the process of law or for unfair advantage to either of the party of the case.

All these facts were taken into consideration by the learned trial court while rejecting the application under Section 319 Cr.P.C. which cannot be said to be illegal and inappropriate but this revision being devoid of merit is liable to be dismissed.
